target.name: Dyna Robotics

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $120M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Dyna Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Lindon Gao, York Yang, and Jason Ma that has raised $120M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 9 comparable companies across the Robotics & Manufacturing sector, including 8 private firms at Series B and Seed stages (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Walden Robotics, and others) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement to the $120M raised proxy, yielding $240M. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, Walden Robotics at $1.1B) produces a median implied valuation of $1.7B, with range $1.1B–$2.0B. The wide dispersion reflects heterogeneity in peer stage mix and funding profiles.

Triangulated analysis across both methods supports a valuation range of $204M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $970M. The substantial spread reflects material uncertainty around the appropriate peer comparability and stage-progression assumptions. Key sensitivities include: peer selection within the robotics frontier-tech universe; timing and likelihood of Series B/C progression; and capital intensity relative to near-stage peer cohorts.
